svg.title: Thirty Days to a Defensible Acquisition Pipeline
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-thirty-day-evidence-sprint; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: Thirty Days to a Defensible Acquisition Pipeline; subtitle: Four weekly milestones produce evidence, not an assumed first closing; chapter number: 12; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: The first sprint establishes a working acquisition system. A first completed deal remains a 2–6 month planning horizon. Weekly activity targets are illustrative and separate from the mature annual cohort used in the funnel.; caption: End the month with priced, documented opportunities and explicit unresolved conditions; do not accelerate execution by skipping lender, permit, or environmental work.; stages: label: Days 1-7; value: Choose one market and map 50 parcels; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Select a primary revenue rail and buyer profile. Load FCC ASR or state DOT AADT layers into QGIS, verify local use criteria, and create parcel records with source dates and ownership evidence.; label: Days 8-14; value: Screen 20 parcels and seek 10 owner conversations; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Prioritize transferable rights and demonstrated buyer demand. Request leases and amendments, document owner authority, and record exclusion reasons without treating outreach targets as achieved conversions.; label: Days 15-21; value: Price three candidates and assemble diligence scopes; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Model downside rent and termination assumptions, request buyer indications, identify lender requirements, and obtain title, Phase I, survey, or permit work proposals appropriate to each candidate.; label: Days 22-30; value: Advance one conditional control package; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Negotiate a diligence-contingent option or equivalent control structure, assign consent owners, and schedule specialist work. Test settlement and billing ledgers using synthetic entries; execute no IOS master lease before environmental and heavy-axle checks.

text.title: Thirty Days to a Defensible Acquisition Pipeline
text.tspan: Thirty Days to a Defensible Acquisition Pipeline

circle.title: label: Days 1-7; value: Choose one market and map 50 parcels; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Select a primary revenue rail and buyer profile. Load FCC ASR or state DOT AADT layers into QGIS, verify local use criteria, and create parcel records with source dates and ownership evidence.

text.title: Choose one market and map 50 parcels

circle.title: label: Days 8-14; value: Screen 20 parcels and seek 10 owner conversations; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Prioritize transferable rights and demonstrated buyer demand. Request leases and amendments, document owner authority, and record exclusion reasons without treating outreach targets as achieved conversions.

text.title: Screen 20 parcels and seek 10 owner conversations

circle.title: label: Days 15-21; value: Price three candidates and assemble diligence scopes; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Model downside rent and termination assumptions, request buyer indications, identify lender requirements, and obtain title, Phase I, survey, or permit work proposals appropriate to each candidate.

text.title: Price three candidates and assemble diligence scopes

circle.title: label: Days 22-30; value: Advance one conditional control package; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Negotiate a diligence-contingent option or equivalent control structure, assign consent owners, and schedule specialist work. Test settlement and billing ledgers using synthetic entries; execute no IOS master lease before environmental and heavy-axle checks.

text.title: Assumptions: The first sprint establishes a working acquisition system. A first completed deal remains a 2–6 month planning horizon. Weekly activity targets are illustrative and separate from the mature annual cohort used in the funnel.
text.tspan: Assumptions: The first sprint establishes a working acquisition system. A first completed deal remains a 2–6 month planning horizon.
Weekly activity targets are illustrative and separate from the mature annual cohort used in the funnel.

text.title: Ordinal roadmap: spacing represents sequence, not elapsed time.
